title: Meeting the Family
description: Polite Japanese for a partner’s parents and relatives, and anyone you want to make a good first impression on.

phrases.japanese: はじめまして。お会いできてうれしいです

furigana.b: いできてうれしいです

phrases.english: Nice to meet you. I’m so glad to meet you.
phrases.registerNotes: お会いできて is the humble “getting to meet you”: warm and respectful at once.

phrases.japanese: いつもお世話になっています
phrases.english: Thank you for all you do for us.
phrases.registerNotes: The standard greeting to people who look after you or your partner. It’s said even on a first meeting, for what they do for your partner.

phrases.japanese: 今日はお招きいただき、ありがとうございます

furigana.b: きいただき、ありがとうございます

phrases.romaji: kyō wa o-maneki itadaki, arigatō gozaimasu
phrases.english: Thank you for inviting me today.
phrases.registerNotes: Thanks for the invitation, in polite Japanese. Say it on arrival, after the greeting.

phrases.japanese: つまらないものですが、どうぞ

furigana.b: つまらないものですが、どうぞ

phrases.english: It’s just a little something, but please.
phrases.registerNotes: Handing over a gift (literally “it’s a boring thing”). Many people now say ほんの気持ちですが (“just a token”), which sounds warmer.
Said as you step inside someone’s home, just after taking your shoes off at the door.

phrases.english: Please don’t go to any trouble.
phrases.registerNotes: When your hosts start fussing over drinks and food. They will anyway; it’s part of the dance.

phrases.japanese: 何かお手伝いしましょうか
phrases.registerNotes: Offering to help in the kitchen or with clearing up. The humble お〜する is right for a partner’s family.

phrases.japanese: とてもおいしいです。お料理がお上手ですね

furigana.b: とてもおいしいです。お

phrases.romaji: totemo oishii desu, o-ryōri ga o-jōzu desu ne
phrases.english: It’s delicious. You’re a wonderful cook.
phrases.registerNotes: Praising the cooking is always welcome. Expect them to say that it’s nothing special.

phrases.japanese: もう十分いただきました
phrases.registerNotes: Turning down seconds politely. If you clear your plate, they may keep refilling it; leave a little to show you’re full.

phrases.japanese: 日本語はまだ勉強中です
phrases.registerNotes: Sets expectations kindly, and usually earns encouragement. They’ll likely say 上手ですね anyway.

phrases.japanese: ゆっくり話していただけますか
phrases.registerNotes: More respectful than ゆっくり話してください: right for older relatives.

phrases.japanese: これからよろしくお願いいたします
phrases.english: I look forward to getting to know you all.
phrases.registerNotes: The formal close to a first meeting with a family. いたします is the humble します.
Said at the door as you leave (literally “I intruded”). Add 今日はありがとうございました.
